The history of amoxicillin-clavulanic acid use is less likely to be the cause, as drug-induced liver injury from this antibiotic typically presents with a different pattern of enzyme elevation and is less common. The positive Anti-HBs and Anti-HBc indicate past hepatitis B infection, not acute hepatitis B, which is consistent with the serology findings. Ultrasound findings of grade I steatosis suggest mild fatty liver, which is unlikely to cause the severe enzyme elevation observed. Drug-induced cholestasis is also a possibility but less likely given the specific enzyme pattern and recent steroid use.
